title: Multiplicity of at least k normalized solutions for the L^2-subcritical fractional Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson system with critical growth (Theorem 1.1)
author: Yu-Qin Zhao; Jia-Feng Liao
work: Normalized solutions for a fractional Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson systems with critical growth
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026 (2026), No. 03, pp. 1--27; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.03; publisher version
difficulty_reason: The stated proof of Theorem 1.1 (lines 1207--1216) is deliberately a two-line reduction, and the whole weight of the unit sits in the chain it closes over: Lemma 3.5 (source lem4.5) proves that the genus of the critical set at a repeated level is at least l+1, and its proof needs Lemma 3.4 plus Lemma 3.3 (source lem2.161, lines 588--1153), which is a complete source-local compactness machine. Lemma 3.3 has to truncate the L^2-supercritical term to keep I_{mu,tau} bounded below on S_r(c), show that critical points of the truncated functional above a threshold are critical points of the original I_mu, and then establish the (PS)_d condition below level 0 for large mu by estimating the Lagrange multiplier lambda_n finely, invoking the radial concentration-compactness principle at the critical exponent 2*_s, and using the Pohozaev identity to exclude the critical concentration level. Multiplicity then comes from genus theory. Concentration-compactness, the Pohozaev identity and the genus are named prerequisites, but the truncation threshold, the multiplier estimate and the exclusion of the critical level are new and specific to this Kirchhoff-Schrodinger-Poisson system; this is research-level analysis well beyond any qualifying examination.
